# kinsta_primary_domain (Resource)

Sets an environment's primary domain. The domain must already be a domain of the environment (see `kinsta_site_domain`). Destroying this resource leaves the primary domain as it is and only removes it from Terraform state, since an environment always has a primary domain.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "kinsta_primary_domain" "blog" {
  site_id        = kinsta_site.blog.id
  environment_id = kinsta_site.blog.live_environment_id
  domain_name    = kinsta_site_domain.apex.domain_name

  # Rewrite the old URL to the new one in the WordPress database.
  run_search_and_replace = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain_name` (String) Domain to make primary, lowercase and without a trailing dot.
- `environment_id` (String) ID of the environment.
- `site_id` (String) ID of the site the environment belongs to.

### Optional

- `run_search_and_replace` (Boolean) Whether Kinsta rewrites the old primary URL to the new one in the WordPress database when the primary domain changes. Defaults to `true`. Only used when a change is made.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `environment_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by <site_id>/<environment_id>.
terraform import kinsta_primary_domain.blog 0f7a3e1c-0000-4000-8000-000000000000/7d2b9c44-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
```
